title: Heat units: calorie and joule (তাপের একক: ক্যালরি ও জুল)
placement: Book page 161, topic 6.1 (তাপ ও তাপমাত্রা): the page has no picture, so this goes next to the paragraph on the units of heat ('তাপের আরো একটি একক আছে, তার নাম ক্যালরি (cal)। 1 gm পানির তাপমাত্রা 1°C বাড়াতে হলে যে পরিমাণ তাপের দরকার সেটা হচ্ছে 1 ক্যালরি। 1 ক্যালরি হচ্ছে 4.2 J এর সমান') and the food-calorie remark after it.
description: The units of heat (page 161, topic 6.1) on a lab bench with a slate-blue top in front of a warm beige wall: a small glass beaker of water (one gram) on a steel stand over three burner flames, and a big thermometer beside it whose enamel scale counts how many °C the water has risen (0 to 5, in Bangla digits). One button gives 1 calorie of heat at a time (up to 5): the flames flare, the red column rises exactly 1°C per calorie, and the panel keeps the sum (n cal = n × 4.2 J, calories orange, joules violet) with the book's equation 1 ক্যালরি (cal) = 4.2 জুল (J) under it. The rule grows in the book's words: the heat that raises 1 gm of water by 1°C is 1 calorie; heat is energy so its unit is the joule, another unit is the calorie; the food calorie is k cal, that is 1000 calories. Test tab: 5 questions (1 calorie in joules; the heat for 1 gm of water 1°C; calories and joules for the temperature rise read off the thermometer; the food calorie in calories), every wrong choice a real mistake with its own note. Phone-first, Bangla and English. The molecules of heat are in the sister figure heat-molecules.
